statement: Agent Quality Toolkit supports quality-management practices; it is not a validated system and does not by itself make any process compliant with GMP, GDP, 21 CFR Part 11 or EU Annex 11.

spec.envelope.description: Evidence envelope with actor and role, action, subject, before/after, UTC time and zone, reason and meaning

spec.canonical-hash.description: Canonical JSON and SHA-256 record hashes; strict parsing (no floats, no duplicate keys)

spec.signature.description: Ed25519 record signatures and detached signed statements bound to a content hash

spec.chain.description: Hash chain over stored records (edit, insert, delete and reorder become visible)

spec.checkpoint.description: Signed checkpoints of the chain head for storage outside the writer

spec.conformance.description: Open specification, JSON Schemas, conformance levels L1-L3 and test vectors

spec.human-check.description: Shared agent-context check for human-only decisions; refusals recorded as <tool>.refused

trail.writer.description: Separate append-only writer service with service time and OS process attribution (observed)

trail.spool-gap.description: Client spool while the writer is down; gap markers instead of silent loss

trail.anchor.description: RFC 3161 timestamps and exported heads anchoring checkpoints outside the writer

trail.import.description: Idempotent importers for Claude Code hooks and Claude Code, Codex and pi session logs

trail.verify-export.description: Verification (intact / broken from seq N), JSONL export with keys and checkpoints, readable report

trail.alcoa.description: ALCOA++ report per record and in aggregate, citing catalogue IDs

trail.review.description: Risk-based audit-trail review with saved queries, reviewer independence enforced, signed review record

signoff.signature.description: Signature with meaning, printed name, time and zone bound to the exact content hash; manifestation

signoff.reauth.description: Re-authentication (passphrase) at every signing; failed attempts recorded

signoff.invalidation.description: A signature visibly stops applying when the signed content changes or is withdrawn

signoff.identity.description: Unique, never reused signer IDs; key enrolment, revocation and compromise dates

signoff.policy.description: Signature policy per meaning (roles, minimum signatures, author differs from approver)

signoff.approved-actions.description: Prepare, approve exact hash, claim once, record outcome; unknown outcomes never retried

change.plan-ledger.description: Hash-reconciled plans; unreconciled edits block finish

change.receipts.description: Runner-captured verification receipts with staleness and anti-gaming warnings

change.finish.description: Finish gate requiring fresh passing receipts; scoped commit with trailers

change.review.description: Review records with reviewer independence class and verdict bound to the diff hash

change.reconcile-diff.description: Approved-versus-actual comparison of declared paths and the real diff

change.trace-report.description: Trace report from requirement and task to commits, receipts, reviews and sign-off; gate JSON

sensei.read-only-advisor.description: Advisor agent of any vendor in an OS sandbox that cannot change the project

sensei.advice-ledger.description: Every consultation on record (content hash and excerpt) with owner decisions

sensei.owner-control.description: Owner modes (manual, confirm, auto) and budgets; authenticated owner operations

quarantine.hold.description: Untrusted inputs scored and held in risk bands; content withheld until a decision

quarantine.release.description: Release, trusted source and declared threat decided by a responsible person with a reason

quarantine.cases.description: Case files with evidence spans, detector and threshold versions and decision history

quarantine.self-trust-guard.description: Decisions refused when run from an agent session; refusals recorded

validate.detector.description: Detector validation with calibrated thresholds and exact binomial confidence bounds

validate.reviewer.description: AI reviewer qualification on seeded defects with detection, false alarms and repeatability

validate.protocol-lock.description: Acceptance criteria fixed and hashed before the run

validate.qualification.description: Human qualification decision with validity period and requalification triggers

capa.intake.description: Deviations recorded by hand or accepted from evidence-based candidates

capa.investigation.description: Structured root-cause investigation (5 Whys, Ishikawa categories) with evidence links

capa.action.description: Corrective and preventive changes to agent controls with before/after hashes and approval

capa.effectiveness.description: Effectiveness criteria evaluated from evidence; closure only when effective or justified

capa.trends.description: Trend review of deviations and CAPAs for management review

source.document: EU GMP Chapter 4 consultation draft (July 2025), Table 1 and glossary; PIC/S PI 041-1 (2021); MHRA GxP Data Integrity Guidance and Definitions (2018)
source.version: Chapter 4 consultation draft, July 2025 ("Traceable" added to ALCOA+)
source.basis: Attribute meanings checked against Table 1 of the Chapter 4 consultation draft https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/fa336a6e-753b-46fc-b53b-9178bacd8878_en?filename=mp_vol4_chap4_consultation_guideline_en.pdf; paraphrased in own words. The PIC/S and MHRA definitions were not re-checked in this pass.

items.title: Attributable
items.paraphrase: It is clear which person or computerised system performed a recorded task and when, and for any change to a record who made it, when and why.
items.user_must: Give every person and agent session its own identity; do not share accounts or keys.

items.title: Legible
items.paraphrase: Records are readable and unambiguous, including all original entries; where search, query or trending matters to the meaning of electronic data, it stays usable through a suitable application.
items.user_must: Keep the export and report tools available for the retention period.

items.title: Contemporaneous
items.paraphrase: Actions, events and decisions are recorded as they take place, including what was decided and why, not reconstructed later.
items.user_must: Route tool records to the trail service as they happen; review gap markers.

items.title: Original
items.paraphrase: The first capture of the information (or a true copy) is kept, and information captured in a dynamic state remains available in that state.
items.user_must: Keep the original session logs where they matter; the trail stores hashes and excerpts, not full content.

items.title: Accurate
items.paraphrase: Records truthfully represent the facts; accuracy rests on qualified and validated equipment and systems, controlled procedures and data review, deviation management and trained staff.
items.user_must: Verify the trail regularly and investigate any break.

items.title: Complete
items.paraphrase: All information needed to recreate an event is present, at a level of detail matching its criticality, nothing is lost or deleted, and electronic records include their relevant metadata.
items.user_must: Send all relevant tool output to the trail; keep external checkpoints to detect truncation.

items.title: Consistent
items.paraphrase: Information is created, processed and stored in a defined, consistent way, for example chronological sequence, date formats, units and rounding.
items.user_must: Keep host clocks synchronised; use one trail per scope of records.

items.title: Enduring
items.paraphrase: Records stay intact and accessible as durable records for the whole period in which they might be needed.
items.user_must: Back up the trail and its keys; define and follow a retention period.

items.title: Available
items.paraphrase: Records are available in readable form, throughout the retention period, to the people who review them for release, investigations, trending, audits or inspections.
items.user_must: Test export and restore periodically.

items.title: Traceable
items.paraphrase: Recorded identifiers make it possible to follow where data came from, how it changed and where it is held.
items.user_must: Link records (links) when a decision depends on earlier evidence.

source.basis: Checked against https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2016-11/annex11_01-2011_en_0.pdf (EudraLex Volume 4). Paraphrased in own words; clause numbering of the 2011 text, which differs from the 2025 draft.

items.title: Risk management
items.paraphrase: Risk management is applied throughout the system life cycle, taking patient safety, data integrity and product quality into account; the extent of validation and data-integrity controls follows a justified, documented risk assessment.
items.user_must: Perform and document the risk assessment for your use of agents and of AQT.

items.title: Validation documentation
items.paraphrase: Validation documentation and reports cover the relevant life-cycle steps, with standards, protocols, acceptance criteria and records justified by risk assessment. They include change control records where applicable and reports on deviations observed during validation.
items.user_must: Keep the validation documentation of your system.

items.title: User requirements and traceability
items.paraphrase: User requirements specifications describe the required functions, are based on documented risk assessment and GMP impact, and are traceable throughout the life cycle.
items.user_must: Maintain the user requirements and their IDs.

items.title: Test methods and scenarios
items.paraphrase: Evidence of appropriate test methods and test scenarios is demonstrated, considering parameter limits, data limits and error handling. Automated test tools and test environments have documented assessments of their adequacy.
items.user_must: Define the tests that make up your evidence.

items.title: Data
items.paraphrase: Where systems exchange data electronically, built-in checks make sure the data is entered and processed correctly and securely.
items.user_must: Check imported data at interfaces you add.

items.title: Data storage
items.paraphrase: Physical and electronic measures protect data from damage; stored data is checked for accessibility, readability and accuracy and stays accessible for the whole retention period.
items.user_must: Check stored trails periodically.

items.title: Backups
items.paraphrase: All relevant data is backed up regularly; backup integrity and accuracy and the ability to restore are verified during validation and then monitored periodically.
items.user_must: Make backups and run restore tests.

items.title: Printouts
items.paraphrase: Clear printed copies of electronically stored data can be obtained.

items.title: Audit trails
items.paraphrase: Based on risk, a system-generated record of all GMP-relevant changes and deletions is kept; the reason for a change or deletion is documented; audit trails are available in intelligible form and reviewed regularly.
items.user_must: Decide what is GMP-relevant and review the trail at a defined frequency.

items.title: Change and configuration management
items.paraphrase: Changes to a computerised system, including its configuration, are made only in a controlled manner under a defined procedure.
items.user_must: Put agent instructions, hooks and thresholds under your change procedure.

items.title: Periodic evaluation
items.paraphrase: Systems are evaluated periodically to confirm they remain in a valid state and continue to meet GMP, considering for example functionality, deviations, incidents, upgrades, performance, security and validation status.
items.user_must: Plan and perform periodic reviews.

items.title: Security
items.paraphrase: Physical and/or logical controls restrict access to the computerised system to authorised persons.
items.user_must: Configure OS users, permissions and network exposure.

items.title: Identity of operators
items.paraphrase: Data and document management systems capture who entered, changed, confirmed or deleted data, and when.

items.title: Incident management
items.paraphrase: Every incident, including but not limited to system failures and data errors, is reported and assessed; for a critical incident the root cause is determined and drives corrective and preventive actions.
items.user_must: Define what counts as a critical incident.

items.title: Electronic signature
items.paraphrase: Within the company, electronic signatures carry the same weight as handwritten ones, stay permanently linked to their record and show the time and date they were applied.
items.user_must: State in your procedures that electronic signatures are binding.

items.title: Archiving
items.paraphrase: Archived data is checked for accessibility, readability and integrity; before relevant changes to the system, the ability to retrieve the data is ensured and tested.
items.user_must: Archive trails with keys and checkpoints and test retrieval.

catalogues.title: EU GMP Annex 11 — Computerised Systems (revision draft 2025)

source.document: EudraLex Volume 4, Annex 11 Computerised Systems, revision drafted by the EMA GMDP Inspectors Working Group with PIC/S
source.version: draft for stakeholder consultation, 7 July – 7 October 2025
source.status: draft (not adopted as of 2026-10-22; the 2011 text is in force; numbering may change)
source.basis: Checked against the consultation draft https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/40231f18-e564-4043-94de-c031f813d38b_en?filename=mp_vol4_chap4_annex11_consultation_guideline_en.pdf. Paraphrased in own words; where an item groups clauses, its ID uses the first clause.

items.title: Data integrity
items.paraphrase: Data captured, analysed and reported by systems used in GMP activities must be trustworthy; data integrity, as defined by the ALCOA+ principles, spans data handling, identity and access management, audit trails, electronic signatures and security.
items.user_must: Apply the principles to your whole process, not only to the tools.

items.title: Deviations and changes in the quality system
items.paraphrase: All deviations are recorded and significant ones investigated for root cause and impact, with corrective and preventive actions whose effectiveness is verified. Changes, including configuration, hardware, software and platform, are controlled, and significant changes are subject to requalification and validation.
items.user_must: Decide which deviations and changes are significant.

items.title: Requirements and traceability
items.paraphrase: Approved system requirements describe the GMP functionality relied on, are kept current over the life cycle and are traceable to design specifications and test cases. Test cases that do not trace to a requirement or specification do not count as qualification or validation.
items.user_must: Maintain requirement IDs and link them in plans.

items.title: Test evidence and approved plans
items.paraphrase: Qualification and validation follow approved plans, protocols and test scripts and give evidence as executed test scripts and, where relevant, screen captures. They are completed and reported before use, and a conditional approval needs a documented impact assessment stated in the validation report.
items.user_must: Approve plans before execution and keep screenshots where needed.

items.title: Personal accounts and segregation of duties
items.paraphrase: Every user has a unique personal account, and shared accounts are acceptable only for read-only access. Users involved in GMP activities hold no administrative privileges, privileges are the least necessary, and managers confirm access in documented recurrent reviews.
items.user_must: Give each agent session and each person its own identity; review access periodically.

items.title: Access log
items.paraphrase: An access log, separate or within the audit trail, automatically records the username, the role where several can be chosen, and login and logout times including inactivity logouts. It is sortable and searchable, or exportable to a tool that is.
items.user_must: Import session start and end events; host logins remain an OS matter.

items.title: Manual user interactions
items.paraphrase: Any system in which users create, change or delete data, settings or access rights, acknowledge alarms or sign electronically has an audit trail that logs every manual user interaction automatically.
items.user_must: Connect every tool and hook that makes such changes to the trail.

items.title: Who, what, when, why
items.paraphrase: The audit trail captures who made a change (with role where users have several), what changed (with old and new value) and when (date, time and, where applicable, time zone), recorded at the time of the event. When a value changes, the system prompts for and registers the reason.
items.user_must: Require reasons in your tools' configuration where they are optional.

items.title: No edit or deactivation
items.paraphrase: Audit-trail functionality is always enabled and locked, and no user can edit audit-trail data. Changing audit-trail settings or system time, or deactivating the function, itself creates an entry and is possible only for a system administrator not involved in GMP activities.
items.user_must: Run the writer as a separate user administered by someone who does not do the work being recorded.

items.title: Accommodate review
items.paraphrase: Systems support effective and efficient review; all users can sort and search audit-trail data by who, what, when and why in the system, or export it to a tool that can.

items.title: Audit-trail review
items.paraphrase: Audit trails are reviewed under a documented procedure by people not directly involved, targeted by risk, in time for the decision (before batch release unless justified) and available to the QP at release. Review tools are encouraged, and significant variations are fully investigated and recorded.
items.user_must: Write the review procedure, set its frequency and assign independent reviewers.

items.title: Electronic copy
items.paraphrase: A complete electronic copy of system data, including audit-trail data, can be obtained; flat or locked files are not acceptable because the data must remain searchable and sortable.

items.title: Open systems
items.paraphrase: Where the system owner does not fully control system access (open systems), or other legislation requires it, electronic signatures also meet applicable national and international requirements such as trusted services.
items.user_must: Use qualified trust services where your context requires them.

items.title: Re-authentication, date and time, meaning and manifestation
items.paraphrase: Signing enforces a full re-authentication at least as strong as login (password or biometrics alone suffice for further signatures in immediate sequence), logs date, time and zone, and prompts for the meaning. The displayed or printed manifestation shows full name, username, role where applicable, meaning, and date and time of signing.

items.title: Unbreakable link
items.paraphrase: Electronic signatures are permanently linked to their records; a signed record either cannot be modified or, if changed later, clearly appears as unsigned.

items.title: Hybrid solution
items.paraphrase: If a wet-ink signature on paper signs an electronic record, measures give high certainty that any change to the record invalidates the signature, for example by printing the record's hash on the signature page.
items.user_must: Print the content hash on any paper signature page you still use.

items.title: Periodic reviews and unapproved changes
items.paraphrase: Periodic reviews confirm the system stays fit for intended use and validated; they cover changes since the last review, including identifying undocumented changes for example by configuration auditing, and follow up audits, CAPA, audit-trail and access reviews. Their frequency is risk-based and they run to plan.
items.user_must: Schedule periodic reviews and act on unapproved changes.

items.title: Backup and archiving
items.paraphrase: Data and metadata are backed up regularly, kept physically and logically apart from the original, with documented restore tests; completed GMP data and audit trails are protected as read-only or archived. Moves are verified, for example by checksum, before deletion, and archived data stays retrievable in a searchable, sortable form.
items.user_must: Back up, archive and test restores.

catalogues.title: 21 CFR Part 11 — Electronic records; electronic signatures

source.document: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 21, Part 11 (62 FR 13464, 20 March 1997, as amended)
source.version: eCFR text current on 2026-10-22 (last amended 88 FR 13018, 2 March 2023)
source.basis: Checked against https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-A/part-11 (eCFR). Paraphrased in own words; titles of lettered paragraphs are short AQT labels, the CFR gives headings only per section.

items.title: Validation
items.paraphrase: Systems are validated for accuracy, reliability and consistent intended performance, and can discern invalid or altered records.
items.user_must: Validate your own system for its intended use; AQT itself is not a validated system.

items.title: Accurate and complete copies
items.paraphrase: The system can produce accurate and complete copies in human-readable and electronic form for inspection.
items.user_must: Define how copies are provided to inspectors.

items.title: Protection of records
items.paraphrase: Records are protected so that they can be retrieved accurately and readily throughout the retention period.
items.user_must: Back up records and keys; define retention.

items.title: Limited system access
items.paraphrase: Access to the system is limited to authorised individuals.
items.user_must: Run agents and the trail writer under separate OS users where possible; manage accounts and file permissions.

items.title: Audit trail
items.paraphrase: The system keeps secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails that independently capture when operators enter data or create, modify or delete records, and changes never obscure earlier information. The trail is kept at least as long as the records and is available for agency review and copying.
items.user_must: Route all relevant actions to the trail and keep it for the retention period of the records.

items.title: Operational system checks
items.paraphrase: Checks enforce the permitted sequence of steps and events where sequencing matters.
items.user_must: Define which sequences are mandatory in your procedures.

items.title: Authority checks
items.paraphrase: Authority checks let only authorised individuals use the system, sign electronically, reach the operation or its input and output devices, alter records or carry out the operation in question.
items.user_must: Decide who is authorised for which meaning; the agent-context check is a guard, not a security boundary.

items.title: Device checks
items.paraphrase: Device (for example terminal) checks determine, as appropriate, the validity of the source of data input or operational instructions.
items.user_must: Review observed process attribution for unexpected sources.

items.title: Education, training and experience
items.paraphrase: People who develop, maintain or use the system have the education, training and experience for their tasks.
items.user_must: Keep training records for people; AI reviewer qualification is an analogy and does not replace them.

items.title: Accountability policy
items.paraphrase: Written policies hold individuals accountable and responsible for actions taken under their electronic signatures, to deter record and signature falsification.
items.user_must: Write and train the signature accountability policy.

items.title: Control of system documentation
items.paraphrase: Distribution of, access to and use of system operation and maintenance documentation are controlled, and revision and change control keeps a time-sequenced audit trail of its changes.
items.user_must: Keep system documentation under change control.

items.title: Controls for open systems
items.paraphrase: Open systems ensure authenticity, integrity and, as appropriate, confidentiality from creation to receipt, using the closed-system controls where appropriate plus measures such as document encryption and digital signature standards.
items.user_must: Use encrypted transport and qualified trust services where your context requires them.

items.title: Signature manifestations
items.paraphrase: Signed electronic records show the printed name of the signer, the date and time of signing and the meaning of the signature (such as review, approval, responsibility or authorship).
items.user_must: Define the meanings used in your process.

items.title: Manifestation under record controls
items.paraphrase: Name, date and time and meaning are controlled like the record itself and appear in every human-readable form of it.
items.user_must: Use the rendered signature block whenever a signed record is displayed or printed.

items.title: Signature/record linking
items.paraphrase: Electronic signatures, and handwritten signatures applied to electronic records, are bound to their records so that ordinary means cannot cut, copy or move them to falsify a record.
items.user_must: Verify signatures against pinned keys, not against whatever key a record names.

items.title: Unique signatures
items.paraphrase: Each electronic signature belongs to one individual and is never reused by or reassigned to anyone else.
items.user_must: Never share signing keys or passphrases.

items.title: Identity verification
items.paraphrase: Before granting a person an electronic signature or any part of one, the organisation verifies who that person is.
items.user_must: Verify identity before enrolling a signer.

items.title: Certification to FDA
items.paraphrase: Before or at the time of use, persons using electronic signatures certify to FDA that they are intended to be the legally binding equivalent of handwritten signatures, and on request confirm this for a specific signature.
items.user_must: Submit the certification where required.

items.title: Two identification components
items.paraphrase: Signatures not based on biometrics use at least two distinct identification components, such as an ID code and a password. Within one continuous period of controlled access the first signing uses all components and later ones at least one owner-only component; otherwise every signing uses all components.
items.user_must: Choose strong passphrases and protect key files.

items.title: Use only by genuine owners
items.paraphrase: Signatures are used only by their genuine owners.
items.user_must: Keep keys out of agent reach; the agent-context check does not stop a determined same-user process.

items.title: Collaboration needed for misuse
items.paraphrase: Signatures are administered so that use by someone other than the owner needs the collaboration of two or more people.
items.user_must: Organise key custody accordingly.

items.title: Unique ID and password combinations
items.paraphrase: No two individuals have the same combination of identification code and password.
items.user_must: Enforce unique signer IDs in your enrolment procedure.

items.title: Periodic review of credentials
items.paraphrase: Identification codes and passwords are checked, recalled or revised periodically.
items.user_must: Rotate keys and review the signer registry periodically.

items.title: Loss management
items.paraphrase: Lost, stolen, missing or possibly compromised tokens, cards and similar credential devices are deauthorised electronically under loss management procedures, and replacements are issued under strict controls.
items.user_must: Revoke compromised keys promptly with the compromise date.

items.title: Detection of unauthorised use
items.paraphrase: Transaction safeguards prevent unauthorised use of passwords or ID codes, detect attempts and report them at once to the security function and, where appropriate, to management.
items.user_must: Review failed-authentication findings and act on them.

items.title: Testing of tokens and devices
items.paraphrase: Devices such as tokens or cards that bear or generate ID or password information are tested initially and periodically to confirm they work and have not been altered without authorisation.
items.user_must: Test hardware tokens if you use them.

source.document: EudraLex Volume 4, Part I, Chapter 4 Documentation, revision drafted by the EMA GMDP Inspectors Working Group with PIC/S
source.version: draft for stakeholder consultation, 7 July – 7 October 2025
source.status: draft (not adopted as of 2026-10-22; the 2011 text is in force; numbering may change)
source.basis: Checked against the consultation draft https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/fa336a6e-753b-46fc-b53b-9178bacd8878_en?filename=mp_vol4_chap4_consultation_guideline_en.pdf. Paraphrased in own words; where an item groups clauses, its ID uses the first clause.

items.title: Records produced with AI or other automated means
items.paraphrase: The regulated user is accountable for the integrity of documents, records and data produced or processed with AI or other automated means such as validation scripts. Such automated support belongs in the pharmaceutical quality system, whether it runs on premises or as a hosted service.
items.user_must: Inventory the AI tools you use and name the accountable human for each record they produce.

items.title: ALCOA++ data integrity principles
items.paraphrase: Paper and electronic records follow the ALCOA++ principles of Table 1, which add Traceable to ALCOA+. Attributable includes knowing who or which system performed a task and, for changes to records, who made them, when and why.

items.title: Signatures in GMP relevant documentation
items.paraphrase: Signatures, on paper or electronic, identify the signer, carry date and time and a clear meaning such as review or approval, and are indisputable and traceable to the signer and the signed record. A signature policy names the authorised signers, and their role and qualification match the meaning of what they sign.

items.title: Electronic signing of electronic records
items.paraphrase: Records that exist electronically are signed electronically, and hybrid signing is to be avoided. Where paper and electronic signatures exist in parallel, the regulated user defines which one is the regulatory relevant signature.
items.user_must: Sign electronic records electronically; where a paper signature remains, define which signature counts and bind the paper page to the record (see annex11-2025d:13.9).

items.title: Retention of batch documentation
items.paraphrase: Batch documentation is kept for at least one year after the batch expires or five years after QP certification, whichever is longer, and for investigational products five years after the last trial that used the batch. Product-specific legislation may require longer periods.
items.user_must: Set retention periods and reconcile them with data-protection minimisation.

source.document: EudraLex Volume 4, Annex 22 Artificial Intelligence (new annex), drafted by the EMA GMDP Inspectors Working Group with PIC/S
source.version: draft for stakeholder consultation, 7 July – 7 October 2025
source.status: draft (not adopted as of 2026-10-22; numbering and the treatment of generative AI may change)
source.basis: Checked against the consultation draft https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/5f38a92d-bb8e-4264-8898-ea076e926db6_en?filename=mp_vol4_chap4_annex22_consultation_guideline_en.pdf. Paraphrased in own words; where an item groups clauses, its ID uses the section number.

items.title: Scope and human in the loop
items.paraphrase: The annex covers static, deterministic AI/ML models in critical GMP applications; generative AI and large language models are outside it and should not be used in critical GMP applications. In non-critical uses, qualified and trained people remain responsible for checking that their output suits the intended use (human in the loop).
items.user_must: Classify each agent use as critical or non-critical and keep agents out of critical GMP decisions.

items.title: Test-data independence and identification
items.paraphrase: When test data is split from a common pool, staff who develop the model never access it, it is protected by access control and an audit trail, and no copies exist outside its repository. Which data was used for testing, when and how many times is recorded.
items.user_must: Keep test sets separate from training and tuning data.

items.title: Explainability
items.paraphrase: When models for critical GMP use are tested, the system records which features of the test data drove each classification or decision, for example with feature attribution or heat maps. Reviewing whether those features are relevant and appropriate is part of approving the test results.
items.user_must: Treat detector evidence spans as triage aids, not as a full explanation.

items.title: Confidence
items.paraphrase: When a model that predicts or classifies data is tested, the system logs its confidence score for each outcome where applicable. Models have a suitable threshold, and a very low score should be considered for flagging the outcome as undecided instead of giving an unreliable result.

items.title: Operation (change and configuration control, monitoring, human review)
items.paraphrase: Before deployment the model, its system and the process are put under change and configuration control, with justified retest decisions and detection of unauthorised change. Performance and input-data drift are monitored regularly, and where a human decides on the model's input, records of that review are kept.
items.user_must: Record model and configuration versions and requalify after changes.

catalogues.title: EU Guidelines on Good Distribution Practice of medicinal products for human use (2013/C 343/01)

source.document: Commission Guidelines of 5 November 2013 on Good Distribution Practice of medicinal products for human use, OJ C 343, 23.11.2013
source.basis: Checked against the Official Journal text as served by the EU Publications Office (http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/52013XC1123%2801%29; EUR-Lex https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52013XC1123(01)). Paraphrased in own words. AQT applies these concepts to agent inputs by analogy; it does not distribute medicinal products.

items.title: Quality management — principle
items.paraphrase: Wholesale distributors keep a quality system that sets out responsibilities, processes and risk management; critical steps and significant changes are justified and, where relevant, validated, under management's responsibility and leadership.
items.user_must: Take management responsibility for the quality system around agent work.

items.title: Quality system
items.paraphrase: The quality system is fully documented and its effectiveness monitored, with a risk-based change control system. It ensures among other things that records are made contemporaneously, deviations are documented and investigated, and corrective and preventive actions are taken.
items.user_must: Document your quality system and appoint the person responsible for it.

items.title: Management review and monitoring
items.paraphrase: Management formally reviews the quality system periodically, including objectives and performance indicators such as complaints, deviations, CAPA and process changes, and documents and communicates the outcome.
items.user_must: Hold and record management reviews.

items.title: Responsible person
items.paraphrase: The distributor designates a responsible person whose duties include deciding on the final disposition of returned, rejected, recalled or falsified products and approving any return to saleable stock.
items.user_must: Designate the responsible person for releasing held agent inputs; agents never take this role.

items.title: Premises — segregation of products pending disposition
items.paraphrase: Products awaiting a disposition decision or removed from saleable stock are segregated physically or by an equivalent electronic system; falsified, expired, recalled and rejected products are physically segregated at once.
items.user_must: Make sure held content cannot reach the agent by another path.

items.title: Computerised systems
items.paraphrase: Before use, validation or verification shows a computerised system achieves the desired results accurately, consistently and reproducibly, and only authorised persons enter or amend data. Data is protected against accidental or unauthorised change, checked periodically for accessibility and backed up regularly.
items.user_must: Validate your configuration and back up the trail.

items.title: Documentation — general
items.paraphrase: Documentation, paper or electronic, is readily retrievable, sufficiently comprehensive, clear and free from errors; alterations are signed, dated and keep the original readable, and records are made at the time of each operation.

items.title: Complaints, returns, falsified products and recalls — principle
items.paraphrase: Complaints, returns, suspected falsified products and recalls are all recorded and handled under written procedures, and returned products are assessed before any resale is approved.
items.user_must: Write the procedure for handling held agent inputs.

items.title: Complaints
items.paraphrase: Complaints are recorded with all original details; quality complaints go to the manufacturer or marketing authorisation holder without delay, and distribution complaints are investigated for their cause. Follow-up actions, including CAPA and notification of authorities where required, are taken as needed.

items.title: Returned medicinal products
items.paraphrase: Returned products are handled by a written, risk-based process and go back to saleable stock only when defined conditions are confirmed, including examination and assessment by a trained, competent and authorised person.
items.user_must: Define the checks a responsible person applies before releasing held content.

items.title: Falsified medicinal products
items.paraphrase: Identified or suspected falsified products are reported immediately to the competent authority and the marketing authorisation holder, recorded with all original details and investigated. Falsified products found in the supply chain are physically segregated at once in a dedicated area.
items.user_must: Report declared threats to whoever must know (for example the maintainer of a compromised source).

catalogues.title: ISO 9001:2015 Quality management systems — Requirements (clauses used by AQT)

source.version: fifth edition 2015 with Amendment 1:2024 (climate change in clauses 4.1 and 4.2; not used here)
source.status: in force as the 2015 edition; a revised edition was announced for September 2026 (not checked here)
source.basis: Clause numbers and titles checked against public clause outlines of ISO 9001:2015 (https://www.iso.org/standard/62085.html refused automated access; the paywalled ISO text was not consulted). Paraphrases are the author's own one-sentence summary of each clause's intent, not the standard's wording.

items.title: Planning of changes
items.paraphrase: Changes to the quality management system are planned, considering their purpose, consequences and responsibilities.

items.title: Monitoring and measuring resources
items.paraphrase: Resources used to verify conformity are suitable, maintained and, where needed, calibrated or verified.
items.user_must: Treat detectors and AI reviewers as measuring resources and requalify them on change.

items.title: Competence
items.paraphrase: People doing work that affects quality are competent, and evidence of competence is retained.
items.user_must: Keep competence records for people; AI reviewer qualification is an analogy.

items.title: Control of documented information
items.paraphrase: Documented information is available, protected, versioned and retained, with changes controlled.

items.title: Identification and traceability
items.paraphrase: Outputs are identified and, where traceability is required, their unique identification is controlled and retained.

items.title: Control of changes
items.paraphrase: Changes in production or service provision are reviewed and controlled, with records of the review, the authoriser and any actions.

items.title: Release of products and services
items.paraphrase: Release happens only after planned verification is complete, and records show who authorised the release.

items.title: Control of nonconforming outputs
items.paraphrase: Nonconforming outputs are identified and controlled to prevent unintended use, with records of the nonconformity, actions and the authority deciding.

items.title: Analysis and evaluation
items.paraphrase: Data from monitoring is analysed to evaluate conformity, effectiveness and the need for improvement.

items.title: Internal audit
items.paraphrase: Internal audits are planned and performed, and results are reported and acted on.
items.user_must: Plan internal audits; an audit-trail review is one input, not the whole audit.

items.title: Management review
items.paraphrase: Top management reviews the system at planned intervals, using inputs such as nonconformities, corrective actions and monitoring results.
items.user_must: Hold management reviews and record decisions.

items.title: Nonconformity and corrective action
items.paraphrase: Nonconformities are reacted to, their causes determined, corrective actions implemented and their effectiveness reviewed, with records retained.

catalogues.title: EU AI Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (articles used by AQT)

source.document: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), OJ L 12.7.2024, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L 24.7.2026
source.version: text of 2024/1689; the 2026 amendment changes Article 17(2) and the application dates but none of the paragraphs listed here
source.status: in force; the high-risk rules of Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2 Dec 2027 (Article 6(2), Annex III) and 2 Aug 2028 (Article 6(1), Annex I)
source.basis: Checked against http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32024R1689 and http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32026R1744 (Official Journal texts from the EU Publications Office). Paraphrased in own words. These obligations bind providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems; coding agents are usually not such systems, so the mapping is an analogy.

items.title: Automatic recording of events
items.paraphrase: High-risk AI systems are technically able to record events (logs) automatically throughout their lifetime.

items.title: Purpose of logging
items.paraphrase: Logging records events relevant to identifying risk situations or substantial modifications, to post-market monitoring and to the deployer's monitoring of operation.

items.title: Human oversight by design
items.paraphrase: High-risk AI systems are built, with suitable human-machine interfaces where needed, so that people can oversee them effectively while they are in use.

items.title: Abilities of the overseer
items.paraphrase: Overseers are enabled to understand the system's capacities and limits and monitor it, stay aware of automation bias, interpret its output, decide not to use, override or reverse it, and stop it safely.

items.title: Quality management system
items.paraphrase: Providers of high-risk AI systems keep a quality management system documented as written policies, procedures and instructions, covering among others the management of modifications, test and validation procedures, data management, risk management and record keeping.
items.user_must: AQT supports parts of a QMS; the QMS itself is the organisation's.

items.title: Log retention by providers
items.paraphrase: Providers keep the automatically generated logs under their control for a period suited to the intended purpose, at least six months unless other Union or national law provides otherwise.
items.user_must: Configure retention; GMP retention periods are usually longer.

items.title: Log retention by deployers
items.paraphrase: Deployers keep the automatically generated logs under their control for a period suited to the intended purpose, at least six months unless other Union or national law provides otherwise.

catalogues.title: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System (elements used by AQT)

source.document: ICH Harmonised Tripartite Guideline Q10, Pharmaceutical Quality System
source.basis: Checked against https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/Q10%20Guideline.pdf (ICH). Paraphrased in own words.

items.title: Corrective action and preventive action (CAPA) system
items.paraphrase: A CAPA system implements corrective and preventive actions from investigations of complaints, rejections, nonconformances, recalls, deviations, audits, inspections and monitoring trends, using a structured, risk-proportionate root-cause approach. In commercial manufacturing the effectiveness of the actions is evaluated.

items.title: Change management system
items.paraphrase: Proposed changes are evaluated with quality risk management by experts from the relevant areas, against prospective criteria and the marketing authorisation. After implementation the change is evaluated to confirm its objectives were met without harm to product quality.

items.title: Management review of process performance and product quality
items.paraphrase: Management review covers inspection and audit results, periodic quality reviews (complaints, recalls, monitoring conclusions, effectiveness of changes and CAPA) and earlier follow-ups, and identifies improvement actions.
items.user_must: Hold the reviews and record decisions.

items.title: Management review of the pharmaceutical quality system
items.paraphrase: Management has a formal process to review the pharmaceutical quality system periodically, measuring achievement of its objectives and assessing performance indicators such as complaint, deviation, CAPA and change management processes.
items.user_must: Include the agent controls in the periodic review.

catalogues.title: ICH Q9(R1) Quality Risk Management (elements used by AQT)

source.document: ICH Harmonised Guideline Q9(R1), Quality Risk Management
source.basis: Checked against https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/ICH_Q9%28R1%29_Guideline_Step4_2023_0126_0.pdf (ICH). Paraphrased in own words.

items.title: Risk assessment
items.paraphrase: Risk assessment starts from a clearly defined risk question, identifies the hazards, and analyses and evaluates the risks they pose.
items.user_must: Assess the risks of your agent use; AQT's risk queries and bands are starting points.

items.title: Risk control
items.paraphrase: Risk control decides whether to reduce or accept risks, aiming at an acceptable level with effort proportional to the significance of the risk, and checks whether controls introduce new risks.

items.title: Risk review
items.paraphrase: Risk management outputs are reviewed in the light of new knowledge and experience after planned and unplanned events, with a review frequency based on the level of risk.

items.title: Formality in quality risk management
items.paraphrase: Formality is a continuum; higher uncertainty, importance or complexity calls for more formal risk management, and resource constraints do not justify less formality.
items.user_must: Choose how formal your agent risk management needs to be.
